paras: The reported lynching of Pete Megley was a hanging that Nevada papers said had taken place in the cattle valleys of White Pine County in about May 1881, when Megley and another man were rumored to have been found hanging from a tree. Reports blamed ranchmen who suspected the men of cattle stealing, but the story was retracted, revived and denied over several weeks, and no body, inquest or arrest was reported. No report gives the race of either man.

Megley made his headquarters at Antelope Springs, which the White Pine News later called the home of his "cattle-corraling crew," and the Carson City Morning Appeal described him as a butcher of Hamilton. According to the White Pine News, the cattlemen of northern White Pine had long felt "ill-feeling" toward him and had warned him to leave the country, giving him fifteen days to settle his affairs, which he declined to do.

On 7 May 1881 the White Pine News reported that Megley and "a man named Wheeler" had been found strung up to a tree in Long Valley the previous Sunday, while saying it was inclined to discredit the story. A postscript in the same issue said the report was "only one of Mother Kelly's dreams." Rumors spread to Eureka by mid-May, where some named the dead man as Megley and others as Tom Glenn, and the Eureka Daily Sentinel said it did not believe anybody had been hung.

The Eureka Leader passed on several versions placing the hanging in Antelope Valley, Huntington valley or Hamilton, the most credited being a vaquero's statement that he had seen Megley's body hanging on a cedar tree near White River. On 28 May the White Pine News, which had heard that Megley had gone to Wood River, wrote that a local informant had convinced it that Megley and another man were found hanging dead in a valley toward Eureka. In mid-June the Ward Reflex quoted Archie Williamson as saying that the hanging of the two men near Mud Springs, 45 miles north of Ward, was "pretty well established."

On 25 June the Eureka Leader, citing "a prominent cattle man," reported that Megley "was not hung but skipped the country." By late July the Antelope Springs property had been sold to R. Sadler of Eureka and was described as Megley's "former abiding place." No report of a body recovered, an inquest or any arrest appears in the coverage.

The story stayed within Nevada papers, traveling among the White Pine News, the Eureka Daily Sentinel, the Eureka Leader, the Ward Reflex and the Carson City Morning Appeal, with reprints in the Elko Independent and the Unionville Silver State. Each paper treated it as hearsay, under headlines such as "Probably Groundless Rumors," "An Alleged Cattle Thief Hanged" and "Was Pete Megley Lynched?", and the Morning Appeal gave it "for what it is worth."

The tone was often joking and implied little regret: the Sentinel said the Cherry Creek News had contradicted the story while "regretting that it was not true," and that any hanging by "our White Pine friends" would have been for cattle stealing. When the denial came, the White Pine News remarked, "If he only stays away it is immaterial which."

Accounts differed on whether a hanging happened at all, on its place, from Long Valley and Steptoe Valley to White River and Mud Springs, and on the second victim, named once as Wheeler. Those affirming the hanging relied on a vaquero and two town informants, while those denying it relied on a retraction and a cattleman's word, so neither side rested on a firsthand report printed in its own words.

bases: The papers reported, and also denied, that Megley and another man had been hanged from a tree by cattlemen or ranchmen over cattle stealing (A1, A3, A5, A7, A9).

Two informants said the hanging was certain (A5, A7) and a vaquero was said to have seen the body (A3), but the first report was retracted as a 'dream' (A1), the Sentinel disbelieved it (A2), and a cattleman told the Eureka Leader Megley had 'skipped the country' (A9).

accounts.label: First rumor, retracted
accounts.gist: Megley and Wheeler were found strung up to a tree in Long Valley after cattlemen had warned him to leave; before the paper went to press, it learned the story was 'one of Mother Kelly's dreams'.

accounts.label: Vaquero's report via Eureka Leader
accounts.gist: A stock man from Hamilton met a vaquero from White River who said he had seen Megley's body hanging on a cedar tree; ranchmen were supposed to have hanged him for cattle stealing.

accounts.label: Town informants
accounts.gist: A gentleman of the White Pine News's town, and Archie Williamson at Ward, said there was no longer any doubt that Megley and another man had been found hanged.

accounts.label: Cattleman's denial via Eureka Leader
accounts.gist: A 'prominent cattle man' said Megley was not hung but skipped the country.

framing.detail: Local Nevada papers handled the story as an unconfirmed rumor ('Probably Groundless Rumors', 'Was Pete Megley Lynched?') while joking about it and implying approval of ridding the county of a reputed cattle thief.
The Carson City Morning Appeal headed its summary 'An Alleged Cattle Thief Hanged' and gave it 'for what it is worth'.
